result.title: When, Where, How: Active In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
result.summary: Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) adapt to a new task only through the labeled rows in their context. However, labels are expensive to acquire in real-world scenarios due to the need for highly specific domain knowledge to ensure high-quality data. Active in-context learning transfers classical acquisition rules to this setting, in which the model that guides acquisition changes with every label added. We ask how the value of diversity, predictive uncertainty and target-aware information gain changes as a frozen TFM acquires more context. For that, we study Target-Aware Nearest Neighbor (TANN) acquisition and the Expected Predictive Information Gain in Context (EPIC) and evaluate them against classical rules. Our study across twenty benchmarks with two well-established TFMs and classical GBDTs highlights three findings: (i) When: diversity-based acquisition is best during the first acquisition iterations; (ii) Where: labeling pool rows that serve the target inputs via a simple target-aware nearest-neighbor rule matters substantially; (iii) How: EPIC yields the best models at the label budget, retains on average 80--87% of the chance-corrected full-data performance with only 5-10% of the pool labeled on the eight benchmarks with the largest pools, and selects labels that also improve the predictive performance of gradient-boosted decision trees.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究表格基础模型的主动上下文学习，比较多样性、预测不确定性与目标感知信息增益（TANN、EPIC）在冻结模型不断获得标注时的取值变化，并在二十个基准上与经典规则及 GBDT 对照。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时靠多样性、何处做目标感知选取、如何用预期信息增益衡量标签价值」的分解，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与获证价值的评估提供概念类比，但属表格设定，迁移线索需较多核查。
